column1: opentext
ticketmaster is a money hungry monopoly that needs to be stopped.

Generally speaking, Ticketmaster should be compelled to do something to discourage and/or prevent scalping and automated purchasing (bots). I understand they probably don't care though since they get their money either way.

One of the biggest problems with Ticketmaster is the fact that they enable bots to secure tickets. I think that there should be some other way to verify who is actually a fan of an artist, especially someone the caliber of Taylor Swift. There should be ways to cut down on resale so people can’t be selling tickets for $5000 when the face value was 500. But that’s capitalism I suppose.

I got tickets through for the second leg of the north america tour. I will be going to [REDACTED]. I bought these tickets face value through the verified fan drop. 

I think that the way they do things is extremely unfair. Selling all the tickets in a presale is not normally how tickets go on sale and shouldve been communicated ahead of time. Also being placed in the queue at total random. If I did not have a low queue number ([REDACTED]) i would not of been able to purchase tickets. 

I think that taylor should opt for tickets to be non transferable so they cannot be sold on the secondary market. This would eliminate scalpers and the number of people trying to get tickets. Or they can only sell tickets on the ticketmaster platform at face value. I think the blame is on ticketmaster and their practices and on taylor swift + her team for not utilizing this option.

I personally was waitlisted for VerifiedFan and attempted 3 days’ worth of “random” ticket drops prior to the [REDACTED] concerts, but was unsuccessful. However, my sister did get a VF code for [REDACTED], so I did participate in the November presale, and it was an absolute nightmare. The site was locked up from 10am until about 2:30pm Central, and when I finally reached the ticket selection page, everything was wildly expensive and it was really difficult to keep 3 tickets in my cart long enough to click “proceed to checkout.” I cried, I screamed, I had major anxiety, I called my sister to have her calm me down during the process (which ended up being about 35 min). We did end up getting 3 tickets for a “reasonable” price (about $278 each), but when you compare with the Reputation tour, where I had ample time to look at seats and prices, and ultimately settled on floor seats for $160 (that includes fees)… the Eras tour was a nightmare. Ticketmaster failed us as consumers and it’s obvious from how fast the resale tickets hit third party websites that they are only interested in their own profits. They issued a weak apology message and have still continued to fail at preventing bots from entering the queue before real humans, and taking up mass quantities. It’s unfair how I am a massive Taylor Swift fan and have been waitlisted for the Eras tour twice now, while other fans have been able to purchase tickets to several tour dates on a single code, and non-fans/bots have scraped up the majority to turn around and scalp them. The process they used for the Rep tour was questionable in ways (prior to the presale, you’d get points that bump you closer to the front of the queue for purchasing merch from TS website, which is like buying your place in line. But you could also get points by watching her LWYYMD video over and over, which is what I did on repeat during work), but it guaranteed that the REAL fans ended up with a shot at tickets. That’s what’s most important, in my opinion.

My biggest problems getting tickets were my boosts not boosting my spot in line (despite having purchased Loverfest East AND West tickets AND having the TN boost), the queue pausing/kicking me out/displaying error messages/crashing after waiting 4+ hours in line, and finally finding resale ticket sites already selling BLOCKS of seats for my show date before the presale was even over. Any seats on resale sites should have been revoked and placed back into the pool. Other markets, like conventions, have a resale platform that only allows for the resale of face value tickets. Tickets on eBay & resale sites for those events have any been reclaimed and put back into the sale pool for legitimate fans. Ticketmaster charges absurdly high, arbitrary fees, but can’t handle the volume of site traffic they promise they can, and can’t keep tickets out of the hands of scalpers. Truly, what have they done to deserve their place in the market?

I have missed out on tickets so many times. I live in [REDACTED], and Taylor will be performing in [REDACTED] next year. I couldn’t get tickets to my “home show”. It is extremely frustrating and upsetting. I think ticketmaster is a greedy monopoly that should be shut down. They have unethical practices and make the ticket buying process extremely difficult. I hope future tours move to a better “verified fan” system. They way people are verified fans now is just luck. Ticketmaster should our with Spotify and Apple Music to actually look at listening statistics to ensure real listeners get tickets to concerts, instead of tickets going into the hands of bots and resellers.

The only way I got tickets is through my friend's daughter who received a second chance email but already had tickets through another account. 

I would love for
 (a) Taylor Swift to implement some of the same procedures Robert Smith of the Cure did for all future sales through Ticketmaster
(B) find a way to go around Ticketmaster for all sales to her concerts/events. 
(C) Live Nation to be broken up. How they are not considered a monopoly and breaking antitrust laws is beyond me. I believe TM is in cahoots with the third party ticket brokers to pad their pockets, otherwise how would third party ticket resellers have blocks of tickets, by section and row, for sale BEFORE any sort of presale/general sale. I think TM is fully to blame for the ticket fiasco and spending 4 hours of my day on a computer to never even get out of the queue was ridiculous.

Bought tickets from other fans via twitter. 
Ticketmaster supports fraudulent behavior and the verified fan system is flawed and doesn’t actual fans at all. 
My hope is that taylor finds a way to get fans tickets first.

Got tickets through a Sidechat (college social media app) post and then traded for tickets to another date

Ticketmaster needs to do better about bot detection. There are currently few Ticketmaster alternatives because they are a monopoly.

Both times I went to the show I went with a friend who purchased the tickets. I was able to purchase tickets for another friend with my verified fan code for a show I was already going to. I think that Ticketmaster clearly doesn’t care about the fan experience and I wish resale tickets had a cap on how much you could sell them for. Reselling tickets should not be a career

I had a boost through taylor nation, stayed online for hours and failed getting tickets. The only reason I got tickets is where they pick the seats for you based on your price range (I think we should have been able to see the seats before purchasing to be honest). Eras tour showed how terrible ticketmaster is on a huge scale. Even for smaller shows like Harry Styles and the 1975 were impossible to get tickets for, and the “verified resale” is just such a rip off. Also the platinum tickets make no sense for any venue and any artist. I hope in the future they go back to a fans first experience where you gain points to boost your opportunity for tickets.

It would be wonderful to have the system in place that Taylor Swift used for the Reputation Tour. But, I honestly don’t think that’s enough. Ticketmaster should not only be broken up, but it should be illegal for tickets to be sold on any site for more than face value. There would be no need for scalpers to buy tickets (or fans to turn into scalpers themselves to make up money) if no one can profit off the purchase. The incentive structure for that type of action would be cut off.

For the reputation Stadium Tour, Taylor’s team created a “boost” program for presale where fans could purchase merch, watch Taylor videos, etc. in order to get a higher place in the presale queue. This system was very effective in getting tickets in the hands of real fans as it could prove how much someone wanted to see her. Seeing the success of this system, Ticketmaster basically banned artists from using systems like this. Which is why the Eras tour presale went so badly. They don’t care about getting tickets in the hands of real fans because they can profit off of resale & don’t have to worry about any other competitors.

I ended up getting front row tickets buying from a resale site. Bought the last minute. They need to release tickets in waves in the future like they are doing for the 2nd leg. Also more efforts to combat bots. There needs to be Legislation for resale tickets limiting how much you can increase prices.

I ended up getting tickets off of StubHub because after putting SO MUCH effort and time and energy into trying to get them at face value, I couldn't stomach not going to a show. I paid an outrageous amount, which I fully believe is also because of Ticketmaster. There needs to be a system in which people who buy tickets, even just to resell, canNOT sell for an outrageously higher amount than what they paid. This kind of policy seems to be part of the European sales for this tour, and it is ridiculous to me that it cannot also be enforced here in the states. Also, being such a massive, successful company, surely Ticketmaster has the capability to completely block out all the bots being used to buy out and resell tickets. 

One of the most frustrating experiences of my life.
Ticketmaster is a monopoly that should not exist. They need to do better to ensure real fans get tickets at decent prices instead of scalpers and bots.

I was not the one who purchased my tickets. My aunt bought for tickets for around $1,200 off of StubHub on [REDACTED] ([REDACTED] days before our show). I despise Ticketmaster and do not plan on purchasing tickets from their site ever again. In the future. I hope more is done to 1. boost real fans and stop bots and scalpers 2. make the experience smoother and 3. keep prices reasonable. We were sitting in section [REDACTED] and absolutely loved our view and our entire experience. $300 was a perfectly reasonable price for that view and I hope Ticketmaster and other ticket companies can learn from this experience.

I think there is a lot the US gov't could do to prevent these massive issues in the future.  They could make it illegal to resell tickets for more than X amount over face-value for example.  It also didn't appear that there was any real verification that people signing up for verified fan were real people or actual fans.  I was not asked to provide any information that could have indicated I was really a TS fan.  I signed up for  Capital One credit card specifically to get into that presale.  I did get in, but every time I tried to choose tickets I got some kind of error or a message that someone else got those tickets before I could pay for them, and then was kicked out of the queue entirely.  By the time I got back in there were thousands of people ahead of me, and a few minutes later a message appeared that all the tickets were sold out.  The dynamic pricing is also ridiculous and makes it impossible to choose tickets at a particular price point because the price is constantly changing.

I was able to get tickets in the official Ticketmaster process. I do think Ticketmaster should be held accountable for the insane fees they charge and their allowing of scalpers to resell for a ton of money (where Ticketmaster gets to charge fees again). That should all be illegal. 
However, I don’t think any platform could have handled the demand for tickets - there was just too many people not enough seats. I’m not sure how that part could have been done well.
Ticketmaster is a greedy machine especially with unnecessary fees. Ended up getting tickets after all the outrage and they suddenly had more tickets available
I think that Ticketmaster sucks and needs to be reformed

I ended up getting my tickets from TickPick 3 days before the show in [REDACTED]. I also attempted to buy 2 different tickets from StubHub for [REDACTED] but the seller did not send either so I had to get a refund. I hate Ticketmaster for the way they handled this tour, I have been a fan since 2006 and have been to many of Taylor’s tours and was able to get great, face value tickets from Ticketmaster without issue until this year. I really hope something changes so that I will be able to go to her next tour without spending an entire summer’s savings on tickets that are only worth $50.

My biggest complaint with the initial presale is that TM knew how many codes they sent out, and therefore how many people they invited to the party. Then, they acted shocked where there weren’t enough seats at the table. 
They could have staggered the sale so that each city had a different day/time to control traffic.

Also, it was CLEAR once you made it through the queue and into the ticket selection section that bots or automated accounts were purchasing the available tickets. The available seats would show up and as fast as you could click them, they would disappear. I’m the time it took to click a seat, then click ‘checkout’ the seats would be gone and you would get a message ‘sorry, another fan beat you to it.’  A simple timer for the check out process could have prevented this, and is something that TM has used in the past. Once you select your seats, they should hold for you for a reasonable amount of time (7-10 min?) to allow time to checkout. 

The whole thing was a debacle and not indicative of a top-of-their-game company. It reeked if we-have-no-reason-to-care instead.

The number one complaints people have about the their Ticketmaster experiences surrounding the Eras Tour is that it feels nearly impossible to get a verified fan code, and secondly -  that ticketmaster claims to be committed to getting tickets into the hands of real fans, but somehow bots insidiously get a hold of the tickets. Especially with these new “invited fan” or “protected drops” closer to the shows. Many who were waitlisted can’t even get in. It feels like Ticketmaster’s actions rarely benefit their customers in reality. I was able to secure a last minute ticket to my local show because of the day before drop and now I feel hopeless on behalf of fans that are getting locked out of opportunities to have the same experience I was fortunate to have. I attended the [REDACTED] - so the drops weren’t protected yet. I want to see the monopoly broken up so fans have more options to get face value tickets. The other side of the coin is the resale industry, which is nearly as brutal as ticketmaster.

The November release of tickets was an absolute cluster F.  I did not understand how the verified fan registration worked, but I still did it without any real awareness of what I was doing.  I thought I would be able to purchase for any of the shows that I registered for.  Ha.  I only received one code for [REDACTED]  and waited all day to get into that damn queue.  Once in, I could not get any tickets into my cart at all.  It was chaotic.  I didn't sweat it though, because the Capital One presale was the next day and I would be able to get tickets for the [REDACTED] shows- my preferred venue.  Welllll....  I managed to get the tickets into the cart, but Capital One flagged my purchase as FRAUD.  By the time I got that dealt with, the tickets were gone and there was nothing else to purchase.  Never fear, thought I...  the general sale is in two days, I'll get tickets soon.   Welp.  The general sale was canceled and my daughter was devastated.  I ended up purchasing tickets on a resale site at the end of November- nose bleeds for almost $500 each for a show that was much further away from our home than I would've liked to go.  All in all, I spent about $2000 for this experience because I didn't want to let my daughter down...  poor financial choices, but a major payoff with her.  
When it came to the day of ticket drops, it seems bots were able to swoop in and purchase everything before I had a chance to blink.  Clearly, this was not of concern to TM because profits are profits.
Ticketmaster is a garbage corporation who can manipulate the market to ensure higher profits for themselves simply because they have no competition and the government refuses to hold them accountable.

I helped people find tickets through tickets in a fan-to-fan market on facebook. There was a lot of movement there, but scams were also prevalent all over social media. Those scams could have been avoided if tickets were easier for people to buy in the first place.

I asked 5 people to register for VF for the first leg and got one code. I asked 9 people to register for VF for the second leg and got one code. Neither were on my personal Ticketmaster account. The Eventim sales in Europe were extremely well executed and I overall liked the European system better (even those TM ones)

Tickpick, stubhub 

Thanks for highlighting monopolies to Taylor Swift Fans! Let this radicalize them

For the US/China question, not well versed in the subject - there was only “good, bad, or neutral”, so I’m not fully sure and my answer is uninformed.

Ticketing process in other countries was similar. Got waitlisted for England, France (Paris), France (Lyon), Toronto. Similar experiences months later.

Other concerts don’t allow resell or transfer through other platforms. If it was via Ticketmaster only, it could control the resell and thus prices or limit to face value (or within a margin).

Ticketmasters fees and dynamic pricing needs to stop. There’s a mental health crisis in this country. Concerts are a form of entertainment that give people a lot of joy. People unable to afford concert tickets do not get to experience this joy. Joy is a protective factor against depression. Please consider making concert tickets available to all regardless of the race and Socio economic status. Also, there should be consideration by lawmakers into making resale of tickets illegal. Bots are profiting off of this and it is unfair. Also Swift 2024!

'-can we talk about boosts from Taylor Swifts website/fan club?  How did some of us with boosts never receive a waitlist code, and yet those who never received boosts were selected for the fan waitlist. 
- I bought from Vivid Seats.  My “fees” from the concert ticket were around $400.  They base the price of their fees on a percentage of what the seller is charging for their tickets.  Secondary markets should also be held accountable.  There should be market caps in place.  I believe the UK has this. 
-I would love to go again, with actual friends or family this time and not myself.  The concert was absolutely amazing, but sharing it with people would be even better.  Ticketmaster prevented that from happening.

I ended up getting 2 tickets to 1 show via one of the Swiftie Resell accounts on Twitter, [REDACTED]. I had been trying to buy tickets since failing in November and I waited too long after hoping prices would go down on Stubhub before they eventually stayed much higher with demand close to the tour. I felt like my best chance of buying REAL tickets was through the resell fans on Twitter. I read a lot about how to spot scammers and how to protect yourself. I was very close to paying someone who I now believe was a scammer but I trusted my gut based on the word of many Swiftes. I bought tickets within a week before my show, which was not the plan. I was checking resell sites, Twitter, Reddit, participating in radio contests, giveaways, etc. daily for MONTHS on end. I paid $3000 total no tax for 2 tickets in the 200 section and I do not regret it. I completely trusted [REDACTED] and her process, so when she posted those expensive tickets I seized the opportunity before anybody else could. I felt okay spending that amount of money because I knew I was buying tickets from a genuine fan and that they were real tickets. In the months I spent looking for tickets and talking to people (by pursuing a resell post/comment) on various social media apps, I think I came across real tickets only a handful of times. The anxiety I had for months was terrible. But I don’t regret what I spent for the experience I had with [REDACTED] to see Taylor. A lot of the reasons were personal.
I want Taylor to make tickets non-transferable from Ticketmaster (so long as it has the monopoly) so that Ticketmaster can then make tickets unable to be sold above face value.

Ticketmaster changing the public sales the days before the shows into "verified fans" was completely unfair to everyone who's shows already passed. I feel like I would have had a shot had I actually got verified fans for our show. It seemed slightly easier for things I've seen. There has to be a better way to stop the insane resale market.

I spent at least two full days struggling to attempt to buy tickets via the verified fan presale code, and the Capital One presale dates. We experienced website crashes, failure to add anything to the cart, failures to accept payments that were approved, and ended up giving up after days of torture.  Early in the year i got a second chance email that secured me 2 tickets in a selected price range that i could not even pick the seats, but took whatever i got as they were guaranteed to me. 
Ticketmaster has failed the fans, let bots buy and resell the tickets, or bought and scammed anyone buying off of vividseats, who can just take all the profits of RIDICULOUS “fees” and the transfer fees all feed back into ticketmaster. They were not prepared and did not hand out a small enough amount of codes to ensure only FANS would get tickets, let alone leave any fans wanting general sale to have a chance.
Such a shame and Ticketmaster is a monopoly of a ticket sales website that is taking advantage of all.

I got my tickets through Ticketmaster realizing I did not get tickets even though I was verified and had boosts and was given a second chance to through an email. I don’t hate Ticketmaster but I don’t like all the additional fees and how poorly they handled the situation. My hope is that there is a more secure way to get tickets, less chance for resellers to get tickets

absolutely hate ticketmaster, hoping taylor makes her own ticketing service at this point because she already does everything else


down with ticketmaster

I got my tickets from communications made with other fans on Twitter. Without this resource I would not have been able to find tickets. 

I was waitlisted back in November 2022, and when week-of-show Ticketmaster drops occurred, I was still unable to access those sales. Very disappointing since judging from the way people were allowed into prior drops for other cities, there was no rhyme or reason to how TM determined who they gave access to. 

It’s clear that the bots they claim to fight against are actually trusted colleagues and they work together in order to maximize profits made from resale tickets. Highly disappointing that they claim to utilize the Verified Fan system as a way to “beat the bots” yet I, a fan who has attended hundreds of events over the years — a large portion of which were purchased through Ticketmaster — am not considered “real” enough to distribute a presale code to. 

I stated this in the earlier prompt about submitting an FTC report, but I’d like to repeat it here as it is a summary of hopes for future ticket onsales:

Ticketmaster Verified Fans selected for presales should primarily be made up of accounts that have attended Taylor Swift concerts before; users submit a survey as part of the signup process where they list which shows they attended and the subsequent confirmation code from those transactions. 

Ticketmaster already has the info from those purchases and accounts should be pulled from that pool of attendees, with a percentage left open for randomized selections of fans who have not yet attended. 

Furthermore, Ticketmaster should not allow resale of tickets for more than Face Value, and they should limit transfers to strictly within the TM app only, not any outside vendors like Stubhub etc.  

Additionally, there should be multiple reliable ticketing companies that artists can use to sell tickets to fans. No competition is bad for consumers.
Ticketmaster needs to be stopped I still have not gotten tickets for Taylor directly from them and always have trouble no matter what artist I’m seeing.
They’re definitely a monopoly. I am sure they’re working with scalpers and getting a portion of the scalping benefits. Someone needs to really study their revenue.

My friend was randomly selected for the lottery style ticket trop Ticketmaster did a few months before the tour. We were extremely lucky and got our dream seats. However, many concerts haven’t gotten the same multiple rounds of ticketing. I tried to get tickets for Paramore and was unable to obtain any. Dynamic pricing is such a scammy concept too. In recent years, the fees and pricing on Ticketmaster has become ridiculous. I shouldn’t have to drop hundreds of dollars on a concert tickets - just a couple years ago an average seat at a show was under $100.

I attended two concerts. I was waitlisted, but a friend who was not purchased tickets for our group in November. In [REDACTED] about two days before the [REDACTED] concerts I was sent a link to purchase tickets so I was able to get tickets for myself and a friend. I don’t think Ticketmaster broke any laws per se and the problems need to be addressed at the federal level to address the laws they aren’t breaking, if that makes sense, as well as to stop resellers from having access so quickly. And there’s no incentive to stop Ticketmaster from allowing resellers to just continue selling and take fees on every ticket over and over. There’s no reason for them to be taking those fees that used to be for a person when it’s all done by robot.

I’ve been using Ticketmaster since I was 15 years old, and it has always been a huge source of frustration. Customer service is practically nonexistent, and they do not care at all about the consumer. They are one of the greediest companies I’ve ever dealt with. I hope for Taylor’s future tours, longtime fans will be allowed the first opportunities to buy tickets.

I was able to get through the VF presale in November 2022 with a code but everytime I tried to select tickets they were not available. Also I used my sister’s code for an unannounced drop closer to the Santa Clara show. Waited about 90 minutes to get through the queue and there were no tickets. Waste of time.

Ticketmaster should distribute codes more fairly to folks who never got one. Also stop using bait and switch tactics.it would also be helpful to spread out ticket onsale times during the presales so systems aren’t overloaded.

I ended up getting face value tickets hours before the show from a fan who got them during an unannounced drop. Swifties do a good job helping each other out!

I clicked on the first 3 tickets I saw because everything was disappearing. Ended up spending double what I intended and got VIP tickets and then Ticketmaster didn’t send me my VIP boxes in time for my show. It was really disappointing.

Ticketmaster needs to not be allowed to treat real fans like this. My only hope is for future shows the process gets better and bots stop getting tickets first

i was able to get tickets very last minute through a ticketmaster drop, mostly because of grassroots efforts by swifties to figure out the ticketmaster system (not because ticketmaster bothered to tell anyone anything). the organization and information disbursement through social media channels was honestly incredibly impressive and it reminded me why and how people hold so much power, especially when they are passionate about something.

Spending 8 (!) hours of my life in 1 queue only to not be able to purchase any tickets was one of the most soul-sucking experiences I’ve ever had the misfortune of suffering. Then we did it again for second chance “surprise” drops, 1.5-2 hours in the queue for each drop, for a total of ~12 hours spent trying to buy face value tickets, only to fail. I hope I get to see the fall of Ticketmaster in my lifetime.
Thank you so much for working on the situation and gathering the necessary information for something to be done regarding these issues.

I was lucky enough to find my first set of tickets for the first [REDACTED] show through someone on Twitter for face value. Prior to this, I attempted to get tickets through Ticketmaster’s presale November 15-16 for the [REDACTED] shows and was unsuccessful. It was a long, stressful, and incredibly frustrating experience, as was looking for tickets outside of Ticketmaster. I got my second pair of tickets for [REDACTED] on Stubhub for [REDACTED] dollars for 2 tickets, an insane price that no one should have to pay for tickets! My whole family, including me, pitched in for my graduation and birthday present. Somehow during the Ticketmaster drop for all of the the [REDACTED] shows, I was able to get tickets to the [REDACTED] show for a good price. I wish the first 2 presales were that easy. Ticketmaster did not go
through with their statements that Taylor Swift verified fans and fans with boosts would get priority for tickets. They did not have a protected queue like they said they would, and that allowed bots to access tickets. This forced a lot of people to buy from third-party websites, spending way more money than they would if they got them at face value. In the future, I hope Ticketmaster actually prioritizes fans and does not allow bots into their queues. I also hope they do not oversell tickets for a presale, and cancel any future sales because of that. I also hope that Ticketmaster lowers their service fees. Overall, I hope the next experience of buying tickets for future Taylor Swift tours is smooth and not very stressful, and majority of fans are able to get tickets for a decent price and not over a thousand dollars!
If you have any power to make Ticketmaster prevent bots (use recaptcha), or have tickets go to actual fans by requiring the credit card used for entry, it would be good for all
tickets should not be able to be resold on any platforms until very close to showtime

In talking with Ticketmaster, the issue is also with the promoter (AEG Worldwide) and some of the terms they have set in conducting the sale. Just as Taylor was able to change Apple Music based on her leverage and power, I actually wish she was more involved in the fight against the unfair ticketing and presale fiasco experienced by her fans.
ticketmaster is extremely unfair and corrupt. they need to revoke tickets that are for sale on secondary sites.

I only got tickets because i had four people all trying to get just two tickets. Only one person was successful. I had a class when the sale went live and stayed on campus to try and wait out the cue, only to be unable to get tickets regardless and spend my entire day feeling extremely anxious, overwhelmed, and drained. My friend had managed to get tickets for myself and my fiancée and I could not even manage to care because the experience was so miserable on my end.

Ticketmaster needs to be broken down. They will not change because all they care about is profit, so they need to face real consequences for the benefit of both fans and artists. Their fees are unnecessary and absurd considering how horribly run the actual ticket-buying process is.

Ideally, by the time she tours again, something will have been done about Ticketmaster and she can work with people who actually care about fans and artists. Everyday I wish that the smaller-scale bands I’ve can stay small enough to not have to sell through Ticketmaster. It’s a shame.

We only got tickets because of the capital one sale. For the second fall leg we had 9 accounts entered for verified fan and none of the were picked. They do not give this opportunity to real swifties, it shouldn’t be random
ticketmaster sucks and i will forever hate buying tickets knowing that its going through them
US/Canada Ticketmaster should only allow resale at face value like other countries do.

Initially I waited for 3+ hours to sign up for the presale raffle. I was granted a code, but due to problems on the east coast, the west coast presale was delayed from 10am to 3pm(or 2pm??). I waited around all day to be able to buy tickets. I even delayed going into work to try and get tickets, but by the time I got to the map, all that was available were seats behind the stage or VIP. Every now and then, random spots of blue would show up, but by the time I entered to my cart, I was told that another fan got them before me. When she announced the tour, it was stated that tickets would range from $50 to whatever, which is why I initially wanted to go. The only $50 tickets I saw were those behind the stage…I was not about to pay money to see her perform from a screen. I could do that for free by watching livestreams, which is what I ended up doing. Right before the tour began (like in March), Ticketmaster sent me a text saying that I could have the opportunity to get tickets to the show. All I had to do was choose my desired price range and they would choose the best seats for me and charge my card…that seemed too fishy to me and I decided not to do it. I wanted to be able to physically pick and choose wear I was going to sit, not be given a random seat with a “good luck”. I decided to try my luck and wait until my date appeared to try and purchase. I believe right before my date, a queue opened up but again they disappeared faster than they appeared. Later on I saw those exact seats on SeatGeek or StubHub for way more than face value. Now I’m a fan of her, but my persistence on buying these seats was partially fueled by vengeance bc I wasted so much of my time trying to find tickets that I wanted to have something good come from it. I even went as far as following a resale account dedicated to connecting fans with Taylor tickets. Now I’m lucky that I was able to even access all of the maps and that’s simply because I was granted a presale code. I never did get tickets to the tour and ended up watching a livestream on TikTok. I could have went to the venue itself to try and listen but their traffic management is so messed up that it wouldn’t have been worth the hassle. I feel bad for those who had to rely on resale sites because Ticketmaster failed to provide a public sale. They should have never taken away the cart timer because I think that is what really messed people up. However I think the reason why they took it away in the first place is so that they could jack up the prices for their resellers.

I got all my tickets by using my friends verified account. Without her, I probably would have had to pay an insane resale frice.
